quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Unless the young man considers that he

knows me already."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Very much,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"We find, though,

that the Miss Alans were coming, and that we have turned them out. Women

mind such a thing. I am very much upset about it."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I believe that there was some misunderstanding,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Our landlord was told that we should be a different type of person,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"He

thought we should be artistic. He is disappointed."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"And I wonder whether we ought to write to the Miss Alans and offer to

give it up. What do you think?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, stop now you have come,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"So George says. He says that the Miss Alans must go to the wall. Yet it

does seem so unkind."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "There is only a certain amount of kindness in the world,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"That's exactly what I say. Why all

this twiddling and twaddling over two Miss Alans?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"There is a certain amount of kindness, just as there is a certain

amount of light,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"We cast a shadow

on something wherever we stand, and it is no good moving from place to

place to save things; because the shadow always follows. Choose a place

where you won't do harm--yes, choose a place where you won't do very

much harm, and stand in it for all you are worth, facing the sunshine."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, Mr. Emerson, I see you're clever!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I see you're going to be clever. I hope you didn't go behaving like

that to poor Freddy."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No, I didn't,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"He behaved that way to me. It is his

philosophy. Only he starts life with it; and I have tried the Note of

Interrogation first."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"What DO you mean? No, never mind what you mean. Don't explain. He looks

forward to seeing you this afternoon. Do you play tennis? Do you mind

tennis on Sunday--?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"George mind tennis on Sunday! George, after his education, distinguish

between Sunday--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Very well, George doesn't mind tennis on Sunday. No more do I. That's

settled. Mr. Emerson, if you could come with your son we should be so

pleased."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"And then he wants to give up his house to the

Miss Alans."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I know,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You know our cousin, Miss Bartlett,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You met her with my daughter in Florence."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes, indeed!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I--I'll come up

to tennis if I can manage it,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "George, don't go,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"George has been in such good

spirits today, and I am sure he will end by coming up this afternoon."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I do hope he will."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"The old man hasn't been told;

I knew it was all right."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "He has not told, he has not told."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"He has not told his father--to whom he tells all things. It was

not an exploit. He did not laugh at me when I had gone."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"He does not love me. No. How terrible if he did! But

he has not told. He will not tell."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"It is all right. It's a secret between

us two for ever. Cecil will never hear."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"The Emersons have been so nice. George Emerson has improved

enormously."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "How are my proteges?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Proteges!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"You shall see for yourself how your proteges are. George Emerson is

coming up this afternoon. He is a most interesting man to talk to. Only

don't--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Don't protect him."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"It

will not last, this cheerfulness. In January you must go to London to

entertain the grandchildren of celebrated men."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Now play us the other

garden--the one in Parsifal."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Not very dutiful,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, I had no idea!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Our performer has changed her mind,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I vote tennis,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes, so do I."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I vote you

have a men's four."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "All right."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Not for me, thank you,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I will not spoil the set."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Oh, come along Cecil. I'm bad, Floyd's rotten, and so I dare say's

Emerson."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I am not bad."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Then certainly I won't play,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I agree with you, Mr. Vyse. You had much better not

play. Much better not."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I shall miss every ball anyway, so what does it matter?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Then it will have to be Lucy,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"you must fall

back on Lucy. There is no other way out of it. Lucy, go and change your

frock."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I shall want to live, I tell you,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I say, listen to this, Lucy.

Three split infinitives."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Dreadful!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "The scene is laid in Florence."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"What fun, Cecil! Read away. Come, Mr. Emerson, sit down after all your

energy."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"You--and are

you tired?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Of course I'm not!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Do you mind being beaten?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I don't see you're such

a splendid player, though. The light was behind you, and it was in my

eyes."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I never said I was."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Why, you did!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You didn't attend."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"You said--oh, don't go in for accuracy at this house. We all

exaggerate, and we get very angry with people who don't."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "'The scene is laid in Florence,'"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "'Sunset. Leonora was speeding--'"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Leonora? Is Leonora the heroine? Who's the book by?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Joseph Emery Prank. 'Sunset. Leonora speeding across the square. Pray

the saints she might not arrive too late. Sunset--the sunset of Italy.

Under Orcagna's Loggia--the Loggia de' Lanzi, as we sometimes call it

now--'"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"'Joseph Emery Prank' indeed! Why it's Miss

Lavish! It's Miss Lavish's novel, and she's publishing it under somebody

else's name."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Who may Miss Lavish be?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, a dreadful person--Mr. Emerson, you remember Miss Lavish?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Of course I do. I saw her the day I arrived at Summer

Street. It was she who told me that you lived here."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Weren't you pleased?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "to see Miss Lavish,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"No wonder the

novel's bad,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I never liked Miss Lavish. But I suppose one

ought to read it as one's met her."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "All modern books are bad,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Every one writes

for money in these days."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, Cecil--!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It is so. I will inflict Joseph Emery Prank on you no longer."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "How do you like this view of ours, Mr. Emerson?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I never notice much difference in views."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What do you mean?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Because they're all alike. Because all that matters in them is distance

and air."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "My father"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"says

that there is only one perfect view--the view of the sky straight over

our heads, and that all these views on earth are but bungled copies of

it."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I expect your father has been reading Dante,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"He told us another day that views are really crowds--crowds of trees

and houses and hills--and are bound to resemble each other, like human

crowds--and that the power they have over us is sometimes supernatural,

for the same reason."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"For a crowd is more than the people who make it up. Something gets

added to it--no one knows how--just as something has got added to those

hills."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What a splendid idea!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I shall enjoy hearing your father

talk again. I'm so sorry he's not so well."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No, he isn't well."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "There's an absurd account of a view in this book,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Also

that men fall into two classes--those who forget views and those who

remember them, even in small rooms."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Mr. Emerson, have you any brothers or sisters?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "None. Why?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You spoke of 'us.'"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "My mother, I was meaning."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, Cecil--how you made me jump!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I will inflict Joseph Emery Prank on you no longer."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I can just remember us all three going into the country for the day and

seeing as far as Hindhead. It is the first thing that I remember."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Cecil, do read the thing about the view."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Not while Mr. Emerson is here to entertain us."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"No--read away. I think nothing's funnier than to hear silly things read

out loud. If Mr. Emerson thinks us frivolous, he can go."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Mr. Emerson, go and find tennis balls."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Am I really to go?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No, of course not really,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Chapter two,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Find me chapter two, if it isn't

bothering you."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Here--hand me the book."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"It isn't worth reading--it's too silly

to read--I never saw such rubbish--it oughtn't to be allowed to be

printed."
quotes.speaker: Unknown
