quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"'sat pensive and alone. Before her lay the rich

champaign of Tuscany, dotted over with many a smiling village. The

season was spring.'"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "'A golden haze,'"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"'Afar off the towers of Florence,

while the bank on which she sat was carpeted with violets. All

unobserved Antonio stole up behind her--'"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"'There came from his lips no wordy protestation such as formal

lovers use. No eloquence was his, nor did he suffer from the lack of it.

He simply enfolded her in his manly arms.'"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "This isn't the passage I wanted,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"there is another

much funnier, further on."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Should we go in to tea?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I am not coming in to tea--tell mother--I

must write some letters,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "conquered her breakdown."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Something too awful has happened,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Do you know anything about Miss Lavish's novel?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"There is a scene in it. The hero and heroine make love. Do you know

about that?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Dear--?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Do you know about it, please?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"They are on a hillside,

and Florence is in the distance."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "My good Lucia, I am all at sea. I know nothing about it whatever."
quotes.speaker: Unknown
Unknown

quotes.text: "Told her what?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "About that dreadful afternoon in February."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Oh, Lucy, dearest girl--she hasn't

put that in her book?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Not so that one could recognize it. Yes."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Then never--never--never more shall Eleanor Lavish be a friend of

mine."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "So you did tell?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I did just happen--when I had tea with her at Rome--in the course of

conversation--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"But Charlotte--what about the promise you gave me when we were packing?

Why did you tell Miss Lavish, when you wouldn't even let me tell

mother?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I will never forgive Eleanor. She has betrayed my confidence."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Why did you tell her, though? This is a most serious thing."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Cecil happened to read out the passage aloud to me and to Mr. Emerson;

it upset Mr. Emerson and he insulted me again. Behind Cecil's back. Ugh!

Is it possible that men are such brutes? Behind Cecil's back as we were

walking up the garden."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What is to be done now? Can you tell me?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Oh, Lucy--I shall never forgive myself, never to my dying day. Fancy if

your prospects--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I know,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I see now why you wanted me

to tell Cecil, and what you meant by 'some other source.' You knew that

you had told Miss Lavish, and that she was not reliable."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "However,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"What's done's done. You have put me

in a most awkward position. How am I to get out of it?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"He must--that man must have such a setting down that he won't forget.

And who's to give it him? I can't tell mother now--owing to you. Nor

Cecil, Charlotte, owing to you. I am caught up every way. I think I

shall go mad. I have no one to help me. That's why I've sent for you.

What's wanted is a man with a whip."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Yes--but it's no good agreeing. What's to be DONE. We women go

maundering on. What DOES a girl do when she comes across a cad?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I always said he was a cad, dear. Give me credit for that, at all

events. From the very first moment--when he said his father was having a

bath."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Oh, bother the credit and who's been right or wrong! We've both made a

muddle of it. George Emerson is still down the garden there, and is he

to be left unpunished, or isn't he? I want to know."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"You were ready enough at the Bertolini when you rushed me off to Rome.

Can't you speak again to him now?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Willingly would I move heaven and earth--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I want something more definite,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Will you

speak to him? It is the least you can do, surely, considering it all

happened because you broke your word."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Never again shall Eleanor Lavish be a friend of mine."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes or no, please; yes or no."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It is the kind of thing that only a gentleman can settle."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Very well,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"No one will help me. I

will speak to him myself."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Hullo, Emerson!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Found the lost ball? Good

man! Want any tea?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, Lucy, but that is brave of you! I admire you--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Freddy has taken him into the dining-room. The others are going down

the garden. Come. Let us get this over quickly. Come. I want you in the

room, of course."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Lucy, do you mind doing it?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "How can you ask such a ridiculous question?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Poor Lucy--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I seem to bring nothing

but misfortune wherever I go."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Try the jam,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "The jam's jolly good."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No--nothing to eat."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You go down to the others,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Charlotte and I will give Mr.

Emerson all he wants. Where's mother?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "She's started on her Sunday writing. She's in the drawing-room."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "That's all right. You go away."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I can't

have it, Mr. Emerson. I cannot even talk to you. Go out of this house,

and never come into it again as long as I live here--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I hate a row. Go please."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No discussion."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "But I can't--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Go, please. I do not want to call in Mr. Vyse."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You don't mean,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"you don't

mean that you are going to marry that man?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"You are

merely ridiculous,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"You cannot live with Vyse. He's

only for an acquaintance. He is for society and cultivated talk. He

should know no one intimately, least of all a woman."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Have you ever talked to Vyse without feeling tired?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I can scarcely discuss--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"No, but have you ever? He is the sort who are all right so long as

they keep to things--books, pictures--but kill when they come to

people. That's why I'll speak out through all this muddle even now. It's

shocking enough to lose you in any case, but generally a man must

deny himself joy, and I would have held back if your Cecil had been a

different person. I would never have let myself go. But I saw him first

in the National Gallery, when he winced because my father mispronounced

the names of great painters. Then he brings us here, and we find it

is to play some silly trick on a kind neighbour. That is the man all

over--playing tricks on people, on the most sacred form of life that

he can find. Next, I meet you together, and find him protecting and

teaching you and your mother to be shocked, when it was for YOU to

settle whether you were shocked or no. Cecil all over again. He daren't

let a woman decide. He's the type who's kept Europe back for a thousand

years. Every moment of his life he's forming you, telling you what's

charming or amusing or ladylike, telling you what a man thinks womanly;

and you, you of all women, listen to his voice instead of to your own.

So it was at the Rectory, when I met you both again; so it has been

the whole of this afternoon. Therefore--not 'therefore I kissed you,'

because the book made me do that, and I wish to goodness I had more

self-control. I'm not ashamed. I don't apologize. But it has frightened

you, and you may not have noticed that I love you. Or would you have

told me to go, and dealt with a tremendous thing so lightly? But

therefore--therefore I settled to fight him."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"You say Mr. Vyse wants me to listen to him, Mr. Emerson. Pardon me for

suggesting that you have caught the habit."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes, I have,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I'm the same kind of

brute at bottom. This desire to govern a woman--it lies very deep, and

men and women must fight it together before they shall enter the garden.

But I do love you surely in a better way than he does."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Yes--really in a better way. I want you to have your own thoughts even

when I hold you in my arms,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Lucy, be

quick--there's no time for us to talk now--come to me as you came in the

spring, and afterwards I will be gentle and explain. I have cared

for you since that man died. I cannot live without you, 'No good,' I

thought; 'she is marrying some one else'; but I meet you again when all

the world is glorious water and sun. As you came through the wood I

saw that nothing else mattered. I called. I wanted to live and have my

chance of joy."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "And Mr. Vyse?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Does he not

matter? That I love Cecil and shall be his wife shortly? A detail of no

importance, I suppose?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "May I ask what you intend to gain by this exhibition?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It is our last chance. I shall do all that I can."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"You wouldn't stop us this

second time if you understood,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I have been into the dark, and

I am going back into it, unless you will try to understand."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It is being young,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"It is being certain that Lucy cares for me

really. It is that love and youth matter intellectually."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, Lucia--come back here--oh, what an awful man!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Well, he amuses me,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Either I'm mad, or else he is, and I'm inclined to think it's the

latter. One more fuss through with you, Charlotte. Many thanks. I think,

though, that this is the last. My admirer will hardly trouble me again."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Well, it isn't every one who could boast such a conquest, dearest, is

it? Oh, one oughtn't to laugh, really. It might have been very serious.

But you were so sensible and brave--so unlike the girls of my day."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Let's go down to them."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Hullo, Lucy! There's still light enough for another set, if you two'll

hurry."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Mr. Emerson has had to go."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"What a nuisance! That spoils the four. I say, Cecil, do play, do,

there's a good chap. It's Floyd's last day. Do play tennis with us, just

this once."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"My dear Freddy, I am no athlete. As you well

remarked this very morning, 'There are some chaps who are no good for

anything but books'; I plead guilty to being such a chap, and will not

inflict myself on you."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I am very sorry about it,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I have carefully thought things

over. We are too different. I must ask you to release me, and try to

forget that there ever was such a foolish girl."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Different--how--how--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I haven't had a really good education, for one thing,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"My Italian trip came too late, and

I am forgetting all that I learnt there. I shall never be able to talk

to your friends, or behave as a wife of yours should."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I don't understand you. You aren't like yourself. You're tired, Lucy."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Tired!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"That is exactly like you. You

always think women don't mean what they say."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Well, you sound tired, as if something has worried you."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"What if I do? It doesn't prevent me from realizing the truth. I can't

marry you, and you will thank me for saying so some day."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You had that bad headache yesterday--All right"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I see it's much more than headaches. But give me a

moment's time."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"You must excuse me if I say stupid

things, but my brain has gone to pieces. Part of it lives three minutes

back, when I was sure that you loved me, and the other part--I find it

difficult--I am likely to say the wrong thing."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"There are days when one sees clearly, and this is one of them. Things

must come to a breaking-point some time, and it happens to be to-day. If

you want to know, quite a little thing decided me to speak to you--when

you wouldn't play tennis with Freddy."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I never do play tennis,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I never

could play. I don't understand a word you say."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"You can play well enough to make up a four. I thought it abominably

selfish of you."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"No, I can't--well, never mind the tennis. Why couldn't you--couldn't

you have warned me if you felt anything wrong? You talked of our wedding

at lunch--at least, you let me talk."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I knew you wouldn't understand,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I might have

known there would have been these dreadful explanations. Of course,

it isn't the tennis--that was only the last straw to all I have been

feeling for weeks. Surely it was better not to speak until I felt

certain."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Often before I have wondered if

I was fitted for your wife--for instance, in London; and are you fitted

to be my husband? I don't think so. You don't like Freddy, nor my

mother. There was always a lot against our engagement, Cecil, but all

our relations seemed pleased, and we met so often, and it was no good

mentioning it until--well, until all things came to a point. They have

to-day. I see clearly. I must speak. That's all."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I cannot think you were right,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I cannot tell

why, but though all that you say sounds true, I feel that you are not

treating me fairly. It's all too horrible."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What's the good of a scene?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No good. But surely I have a right to hear a little more."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "little more,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Don't open the window; and you'd better draw the curtain, too; Freddy

or any one might be outside."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I really think we had better

go to bed, if you don't mind. I shall only say things that will make me

unhappy afterwards. As you say it is all too horrible, and it is no good

talking."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"But I love you, and I did think you loved

me!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I did not,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I thought I did at first. I am sorry, and ought

to have refused you this last time, too."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"You don't love me, evidently. I dare say you are right not to. But it

would hurt a little less if I knew why."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Because"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"you're the sort

who can't know any one intimately."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I don't mean exactly that. But you will question me, though I beg you

not to, and I must say something. It is that, more or less. When we

were only acquaintances, you let me be myself, but now you're always

protecting me."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I won't be protected. I will choose

for myself what is ladylike and right. To shield me is an insult. Can't

I be trusted to face the truth but I must get it second-hand through

you? A woman's place! You despise my mother--I know you do--because

she's conventional and bothers over puddings; but, oh goodness!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"conventional, Cecil, you're that, for you may

understand beautiful things, but you don't know how to use them; and you

wrap yourself up in art and books and music, and would try to wrap up

me. I won't be stifled, not by the most glorious music, for people are

more glorious, and you hide them from me. That's why I break off my

engagement. You were all right as long as you kept to things, but when

you came to people--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It is true."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "True on the whole,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "True, every word. It is a revelation. It is--I."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Anyhow, those are my reasons for not being your wife."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"'The sort that can know no one intimately.' It is true. I

fell to pieces the very first day we were engaged. I behaved like a cad

to Beebe and to your brother. You are even greater than I thought."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I'm not going to worry you. You are far too good to

me. I shall never forget your insight; and, dear, I only blame you for

this: you might have warned me in the early stages, before you felt

you wouldn't marry me, and so have given me a chance to improve. I have

never known you till this evening. I have just used you as a peg for

my silly notions of what a woman should be. But this evening you are a

different person: new thoughts--even a new voice--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What do you mean by a new voice?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I mean that a new person seems speaking through you,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"If you think I am in love with

some one else, you are very much mistaken."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Of course I don't think that. You are not that kind, Lucy."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Oh, yes, you do think it. It's your old idea, the idea that has kept

Europe back--I mean the idea that women are always thinking of men. If

a girl breaks off her engagement, every one says: 'Oh, she had some

one else in her mind; she hopes to get some one else.' It's disgusting,

brutal! As if a girl can't break it off for the sake of freedom."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I may have said that in the past. I shall never

say it again. You have taught me better."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Of

course, there is no question of 'some one else' in this, no 'jilting' or

any such nauseous stupidity. I beg your pardon most humbly if my words

suggested that there was. I only meant that there was a force in you

that I hadn't known of up till now."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"All right, Cecil, that will do. Don't apologize to me. It was my

mistake."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"It is a question between ideals, yours and mine--pure abstract ideals,

and yours are the nobler. I was bound up in the old vicious notions,

and all the time you were splendid and new."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I must

actually thank you for what you have done--for showing me what I really

am. Solemnly, I thank you for showing me a true woman. Will you shake

hands?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Of course I will,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Good-night, Cecil. Good-bye. That's all right. I'm sorry

about it. Thank you very much for your gentleness."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Let me light your candle, shall I?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Thank you. Good-night again. God bless you, Lucy!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Good-bye, Cecil."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "did,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Since Florence did my poor sister so much good,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"we do not see why we should not try Athens this winter. Of course,

Athens is a plunge, and the doctor has ordered her special digestive

bread; but, after all, we can take that with us, and it is only getting

first into a steamer and then into a train. But is there an English

Church?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I do not expect we shall go any

further than Athens, but if you knew of a really comfortable pension at

Constantinople, we should be so grateful."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "So you're off for a minute, Mr. Vyse?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I was coming to show you this delightful letter from those friends

of Miss Honeychurch."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Isn't it wonderful? Isn't it

romance? most certainly they will go to Constantinople. They are taken

in a snare that cannot fail. They will end by going round the world."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Isn't Romance capricious! I never notice it in you young people; you

do nothing but play lawn tennis, and say that romance is dead, while the

Miss Alans are struggling with all the weapons of propriety against the

terrible thing. 'A really comfortable pension at Constantinople!' So

they call it out of decency, but in their hearts they want a pension

with magic windows opening on the foam of perilous seas in fairyland

forlorn! No ordinary view will content the Miss Alans. They want the

Pension Keats."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I'm awfully sorry to interrupt, Mr. Beebe,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"but have you

any matches?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I have,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You have never met these Miss Alans, have you, Mr. Vyse?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Never."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Then you don't see the wonder of this Greek visit. I haven't been

to Greece myself, and don't mean to go, and I can't imagine any of my

friends going. It is altogether too big for our little lot. Don't you

think so? Italy is just about as much as we can manage. Italy is heroic,

but Greece is godlike or devilish--I am not sure which, and in either

case absolutely out of our suburban focus. All right, Freddy--I am

not being clever, upon my word I am not--I took the idea from another

fellow; and give me those matches when you've done with them."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I was saying, if

our poor little Cockney lives must have a background, let it be Italian.

Big enough in all conscience. The ceiling of the Sistine Chapel for

me. There the contrast is just as much as I can realize. But not the

Parthenon, not the frieze of Phidias at any price; and here comes the

victoria."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You're quite right,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Greece is not for our little lot"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I'm so glad you

only talked about books. Cecil's hard hit. Lucy won't marry him. If

you'd gone on about her, as you did about them, he might have broken

down."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "But when--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Late last night. I must go."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Perhaps they won't want me down there."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No--go on. Good-bye."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Thank goodness!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"It was the one foolish thing she ever

did. Oh, what a glorious riddance!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "garden-child,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Oh, how do you do, Mr. Beebe? Gracious what a mess everything is! Look

at my scarlet pompons, and the wind blowing your skirts about, and the

ground so hard that not a prop will stick in, and then the carriage

having to go out, when I had counted on having Powell, who--give every

one their due--does tie up dahlias properly."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "How do you do?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Here, Lennie, the bass,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Come for a walk with me,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"You have worried them as much

as they can stand. Mrs. Honeychurch, I only called in aimlessly. I shall

take her up to tea at the Beehive Tavern, if I may."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Oh, must you? Yes do.--Not the scissors, thank you, Charlotte, when

both my hands are full already--I'm perfectly certain that the orange

cactus will go before I can get to it."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Yes, Charlotte, I don't want you--do go; there's nothing to stop about

for, either in the house or out of it."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It is terrible, this havoc among the flowers,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"It is always terrible when the promise of months is destroyed in a

moment,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Perhaps we ought to send Miss Honeychurch down to her mother. Or will

she come with us?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I think we had better leave Lucy to herself, and to her own pursuits."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"They're angry with Miss Honeychurch because she was late for

breakfast,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"and Floyd has gone, and Mr. Vyse has

gone, and Freddy won't play with me. In fact, Uncle Arthur, the house is

not AT ALL what it was yesterday."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Don't be a prig,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Go and put on your boots."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"How do you do? Miss Bartlett and Minnie are coming with me to tea at

the Beehive. Would you come too?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I don't think I will, thank you."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No, I didn't suppose you would care to much."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "How delicate those Sonatas are!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Miss Honeychurch!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I met them on the hill. Your brother told me."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh he did?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I needn't say that it will go no further."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Mother, Charlotte, Cecil, Freddy, you,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"If you'll let me say so, I am very glad, and I am certain that you have

done the right thing."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "So I hoped other people would think, but they don't seem to."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I could see that Miss Bartlett thought it unwise."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "So does mother. Mother minds dreadfully."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I am very sorry for that,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "And Freddy minds."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Still, Freddy never hit it off with Vyse much, did he? I gathered that

he disliked the engagement, and felt it might separate him from you."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Boys are so odd."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I have had an

absurd letter from Miss Alan. That was really what brought me over. I

thought it might amuse you all."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "How delightful!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Going abroad? When do they start?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Next week, I gather."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Did Freddy say whether he was driving straight back?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No, he didn't."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Because I do hope he won't go gossiping."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Oh,

do tell me more about the Miss Alans! How perfectly splendid of them to

go abroad!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I want them to start from Venice, and go in a cargo steamer down the

Illyrian coast!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, delightful! I wish they'd take me."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Has Italy filled you with the fever of travel? Perhaps George Emerson

is right. He says that 'Italy is only an euphuism for Fate.'"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Oh, not Italy, but Constantinople. I have always longed to go to

Constantinople. Constantinople is practically Asia, isn't it?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"with Delphi, perhaps, if the roads

are safe."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I didn't realize that you and the Miss Alans were still such friends,

after Cissie Villa."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Oh, that's nothing; I assure you Cissie Villa's nothing to me; I would

give anything to go with them."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Would your mother spare you again so soon? You have scarcely been home

three months."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "She MUST spare me!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I simply MUST

go away. I have to."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Don't you see that I HAVE to go away? I didn't realize at the time--and

of course I want to see Constantinople so particularly."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You mean that since you have broken off your engagement you feel--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes, yes. I knew you'd understand."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Yes, of course; to go to Constantinople until they are used to the idea

and everything has calmed down."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I am afraid it has been a bothersome business,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"No, not at all. Cecil was very kind indeed; only--I had better tell

you the whole truth, since you have heard a little--it was that he is

so masterful. I found that he wouldn't let me go my own way. He would

improve me in places where I can't be improved. Cecil won't let a woman

decide for herself--in fact, he daren't. What nonsense I do talk! but

that is the kind of thing."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"It is what I gathered from my own observation of Mr. Vyse; it is what I

gather from all that I have known of you. I do sympathize and agree

most profoundly. I agree so much that you must let me make one little

criticism: Is it worth while rushing off to Greece?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "But I must go somewhere!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I have been worrying all the

morning, and here comes the very thing."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I must! And the time I shall have with

mother, and all the money she spent on me last spring. You all think

much too highly of me. I wish you weren't so kind."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I must get away, ever

so far. I must know my own mind and where I want to go."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Come along; tea, tea, tea,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "She is playing again,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Lucy can always play,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"One is very thankful that she has such a resource. She is evidently

much worried, as, of course, she ought to be. I know all about it. The

marriage was so near that it must have been a hard struggle before she

could wind herself up to speak."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"she might yet reveal depths of strangeness, if not of

meaning."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"We had much better let the matter

drop."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I wonder."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"It is of the highest importance that there should be no gossip in

Summer Street. It would be DEATH to gossip about Mr. Vyse's dismissal at

the present moment."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Of course, Miss

Honeychurch will make the fact public in her own way, and when she

chooses. Freddy only told me because he knew she would not mind."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I know,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Yet Freddy ought not to have told

even you. One cannot be too careful."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Quite so."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I do implore absolute secrecy. A chance word to a chattering friend,

and--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Exactly."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Have you heard from any Bertolini people lately? I believe

you keep up with Miss Lavish. It is odd how we of that pension,

who seemed such a fortuitous collection, have been working into one

another's lives. Two, three, four, six of us--no, eight; I had forgotten

the Emersons--have kept more or less in touch. We must really give the

Signora a testimonial."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"We shan't have

rain, but we shall have darkness, so let us hurry on. The darkness last

night was appalling."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I have been thinking, Miss Bartlett,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"and, unless you

very much object, I would like to reopen that discussion."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Nothing about the past. I know little and care less about that; I am

absolutely certain that it is to your cousin's credit. She has acted

loftily and rightly, and it is like her gentle modesty to say that we

think too highly of her. But the future. Seriously, what do you think of

this Greek plan?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I don't know whether

you overheard, but she wants to join the Miss Alans in their mad career.

It's all--I can't explain--it's wrong."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I can't see the point of it myself."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"There I cannot agree with you. In it

I spy Lucy's salvation."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Really. Now, why?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "She wanted to leave Windy Corner."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I know--but it seems so odd, so unlike her, so--I was going to

say--selfish."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"It is natural, surely--after such painful scenes--that she should

desire a change."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"So she says herself, and since another

lady agrees with her, I must own that I am partially convinced. Perhaps

she must have a change. I have no sisters or--and I don't understand

these things. But why need she go as far as Greece?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You may well ask that,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Why Greece?

(What is it, Minnie dear--jam?) Why not Tunbridge Wells? Oh, Mr. Beebe!

I had a long and most unsatisfactory interview with dear Lucy this

morning. I cannot help her. I will say no more. Perhaps I have already

said too much. I am not to talk. I wanted her to spend six months with

me at Tunbridge Wells, and she refused."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"But my feelings are of no importance. I know too well that I get on

Lucy's nerves. Our tour was a failure. She wanted to leave Florence, and

when we got to Rome she did not want to be in Rome, and all the time I

felt that I was spending her mother's money--."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Let us keep to the future, though,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I want your

advice."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Very well,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I for one will help her to go to Greece.

Will you?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It is absolutely necessary,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I know--I know."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"She must not stop here a moment, and we must

keep quiet till she goes. I trust that the servants know nothing.

Afterwards--but I may have said too much already. Only, Lucy and I are

helpless against Mrs. Honeychurch alone. If you help we may succeed.

Otherwise--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Otherwise--?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Otherwise,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes, I will help her,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Come,

let us go back now, and settle the whole thing up."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"another

man"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"They that

marry do well, but they that refrain do better."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It gets too dark,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"This comes of putting off. We

might have known the weather would break up soon; and now Lucy wants to

go to Greece. I don't know what the world's coming to."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Mrs. Honeychurch,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"go to Greece she must. Come up to the

house and let's talk it over. Do you, in the first place, mind her

breaking with Vyse?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Mr. Beebe, I'm thankful--simply thankful."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "So am I,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Good. Now come up to the house."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I don't see why Greece is necessary,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"but as you do, I suppose it is all right. It must be something I

can't understand. Lucy! Let's tell her. Lucy!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "She is playing the piano,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Look not thou on beauty's charming."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I didn't know that Miss Honeychurch sang, too."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Sit thou still when kings are arming,

   Taste not when the wine-cup glistens--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It's a song that Cecil gave her. How odd girls are!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What's that?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "All right, dear,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I am sorry I

was so cross about Greece, but it came on the top of the dahlias."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Thank you, mother; that doesn't matter a

bit."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"And you are right, too--Greece will be all right; you can go if the

Miss Alans will have you."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, splendid! Oh, thank you!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Taste not when the wine-cup glistens,

   Speak not when the people listens,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Here's Mr. Beebe."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Mr. Beebe knows my rude ways."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It's a beautiful song and a wise one,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Go on."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It isn't very good,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I forget why--harmony or

something."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I suspected it was unscholarly. It's so beautiful."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "The tune's right enough,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"but the words are rotten. Why

throw up the sponge?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "How stupidly you talk!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "This has been a day and a half."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Stop thine ear against the singer--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Wait a minute; she is finishing."
quotes.speaker: Unknown
Unknown

quotes.text: "I love weather like this,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Vacant heart and hand and eye--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "the better part"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Vacant heart and hand and eye

   Easy live and quiet die."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"But, of course, you know all about these things, and you have Mr. Vyse

to help you. A gentleman is such a stand-by."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "We think it so good of Mr. Vyse to spare you,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"It is not every young man who would be so unselfish. But

perhaps he will come out and join you later on."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Or does his work keep him in London?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"However, we shall see him when he sees you off. I do so long to see

him."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No one will see Lucy off,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"She doesn't

like it."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No, I hate seeings-off,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Really? How funny! I should have thought that in this case--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Oh, Mrs. Honeychurch, you aren't going? It is such a pleasure to have

met you!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"That's all right. We just got

through that time."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I should be told, dear, that I am

unsympathetic. But I cannot see why you didn't tell your friends about

Cecil and be done with it. There all the time we had to sit fencing, and

almost telling lies, and be seen through, too, I dare say, which is most

unpleasant."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "But why shouldn't it be everywhere in no time?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Because I settled with Cecil not to announce it until I left England. I

shall tell them then. It's much pleasanter. How wet it is! Let's turn in

here."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Here"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Oh, well, let it be shop, then. Let's go to Mudie's. I'll buy a

guide-book."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"You know, Lucy, you and Charlotte and Mr. Beebe all tell me I'm

so stupid, so I suppose I am, but I shall never understand this

hole-and-corner work. You've got rid of Cecil--well and good, and I'm

thankful he's gone, though I did feel angry for the minute. But why not

announce it? Why this hushing up and tip-toeing?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It's only for a few days."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "But why at all?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Because George Emerson has been bothering me, and if he

hears I've given up Cecil may begin again"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"My daughter won't

answer me; she would rather be with those inquisitive old maids than

with Freddy and me. Any rag, tag, and bobtail apparently does if she

can leave her home."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You're tired of Windy Corner."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I do not love George; I broke off my engagement

because I did not love George; I must go to Greece because I do not

love George; it is more important that I should look up gods in the

dictionary than that I should help my mother; every one else is behaving

very badly."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Oh, mother, what rubbish you talk! Of course I'm not tired of Windy

Corner."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Then why not say so at once, instead of considering half an hour?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Half a minute would be nearer."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Perhaps you would like to stay away from your home altogether?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Hush, mother! People will hear you"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Of course I want to live at home;

but as we are talking about it, I may as well say that I shall want to

be away in the future more than I have been. You see, I come into my

money next year."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "eccentricity,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I've seen the

world so little--I felt so out of things in Italy. I have seen so little

of life; one ought to come up to London more--not a cheap ticket like

to-day, but to stop. I might even share a flat for a little with some

other girl."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "And mess with typewriters and latch-keys,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"And agitate and scream, and be carried off kicking by the police. And

call it a Mission--when no one wants you! And call it Duty--when

it means that you can't stand your own home! And call it Work--when

thousands of men are starving with the competition as it is! And then

to prepare yourself, find two doddering old ladies, and go abroad with

them."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I want more independence,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Very well. Take your independence and be gone. Rush up and down and

round the world, and come back as thin as a lath with the bad food.

Despise the house that your father built and the garden that he planted,

and our dear view--and then share a flat with another girl."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Perhaps I spoke hastily."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, goodness!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"How you do remind me of Charlotte

Bartlett!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Charlotte!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "More every moment."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I don't know what you mean, mother; Charlotte and I are not the very

least alike."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Well, I see the likeness. The same eternal worrying, the same taking

back of words. You and Charlotte trying to divide two apples among three

people last night might be sisters."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"What rubbish! And if you dislike Charlotte so, it's rather a pity you

asked her to stop. I warned you about her; I begged you, implored you

not to, but of course it was not listened to."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "There you go."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I beg your pardon?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Charlotte again, my dear; that's all; her very words."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"My point is that you oughtn't to have

asked Charlotte to stop. I wish you would keep to the point."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"The

crush when Charlotte gets in will be abominable,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"We shall have to sit three a side, because the trees drop, and

yet it isn't raining. Oh, for a little air!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "He has not told--he has not told."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "CAN'T we have the hood down?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Very well, old lady, stop

the horse."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Is that house to let again, Powell?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes, miss,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Have they gone?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"It is too far out of town for the young gentleman, and his father's

rheumatism has come on, so he can't stop on alone, so they are trying to

let furnished,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "They have gone, then?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes, miss, they have gone."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Certainly,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I forgot it was Friday. Let's

all go. Powell can go round to the stables."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Lucy dearest--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No church for me, thank you."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"A lady to wait,

sir."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, Miss Honeychurch, that you should come!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Miss Honeychurch, dear, we are so sorry! George is so sorry! He thought

he had a right to try. I cannot blame my boy, and yet I wish he had told

me first. He ought not to have tried. I knew nothing about it at all."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "But you must not scold him."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I taught him,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"to trust in love. I said: 'When love

comes, that is reality.' I said: 'Passion does not blind. No. Passion

is sanity, and the woman you love, she is the only person you will ever

really understand.'"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"True, everlastingly true, though my day

is over, and though there is the result. Poor boy! He is so sorry!

He said he knew it was madness when you brought your cousin in; that

whatever you felt you did not mean. Yet"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Miss Honeychurch, do you remember Italy?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I have no wish to discuss Italy or any

subject connected with your son."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "But you do remember it?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "He has misbehaved himself from the first."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I only was told that he loved you last Sunday. I never could judge

behaviour. I--I--suppose he has."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Why, he has behaved abominably,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I am glad he is sorry. Do

you know what he did?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Not 'abominably,'"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"He only tried when he

should not have tried. You have all you want, Miss Honeychurch: you are

going to marry the man you love. Do not go out of George's life saying

he is abominable."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No, of course,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"'Abominable' is much too strong. I am sorry I used it about your son. I

think I will go to church, after all. My mother and my cousin have gone.

I shall not be so very late--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Especially as he has gone under,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What was that?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Gone under naturally."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I don't understand."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "As his mother did."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "But, Mr. Emerson--MR. EMERSON--what are you talking about?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "When I wouldn't have George baptized,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"And she agreed that baptism was nothing, but he caught that fever

when he was twelve and she turned round. She thought it a judgment."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Oh, horrible, when we had given up that sort of thing and

broken away from her parents. Oh, horrible--worst of all--worse than

death, when you have made a little clearing in the wilderness, planted

your little garden, let in your sunlight, and then the weeds creep in

again! A judgment! And our boy had typhoid because no clergyman had

dropped water on him in church! Is it possible, Miss Honeychurch? Shall

we slip back into the darkness for ever?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I don't know,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I don't understand this sort of thing. I

was not meant to understand it."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"But Mr. Eager--he came when I was out, and acted according to his

principles. I don't blame him or any one... but by the time George

was well she was ill. He made her think about sin, and she went under

thinking about it."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, how terrible!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "He was not baptized,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I did hold firm."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"My boy shall go back to the

earth untouched."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh--last Sunday."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"George last Sunday--no,

not ill: just gone under. He is never ill. But he is his mother's son.

Her eyes were his, and she had that forehead that I think so beautiful,

and he will not think it worth while to live. It was always touch and

go. He will live; but he will not think it worth while to live. He will

never think anything worth while. You remember that church at Florence?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"After you left Florence--horrible. Then we took the house here, and he

goes bathing with your brother, and became better. You saw him bathing?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I am so sorry, but it is no good discussing this affair. I am deeply

sorry about it."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Then there came something about a novel. I didn't follow it at all; I

had to hear so much, and he minded telling me; he finds me too old. Ah,

well, one must have failures. George comes down to-morrow, and takes me

up to his London rooms. He can't bear to be about here, and I must be

where he is."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Mr. Emerson,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"don't leave at least, not on my account.

I am going to Greece. Don't leave your comfortable house."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"How good

every one is! And look at Mr. Beebe housing me--came over this morning

and heard I was going! Here I am so comfortable with a fire."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes, but you won't go back to London. It's absurd."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I must be with George; I must make him care to live, and down here he

can't. He says the thought of seeing you and of hearing about you--I am

not justifying him: I am only saying what has happened."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, Mr. Emerson"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"you mustn't. I've been

bother enough to the world by now. I can't have you moving out of your

house when you like it, and perhaps losing money through it--all on my

account. You must stop! I am just going to Greece."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "All the way to Greece?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "To Greece?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"So you must stop. You won't talk about this business, I know. I can

trust you both."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Certainly you can. We either have you in our lives, or leave you to the

life that you have chosen."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I shouldn't want--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I suppose Mr. Vyse is very angry with George? No, it was wrong of

George to try. We have pushed our beliefs too far. I fancy that we

deserve sorrow."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No, please sit still. I think I will sit in the carriage."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Miss Honeychurch, you do sound tired."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Not a bit,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"But you are, and there's a look of George about you. And what were you

saying about going abroad?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Greece"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Greece; but

you were to be married this year, I thought."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Not till January, it wasn't,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I suppose that Mr. Vyse is going with you. I hope--it isn't because

George spoke that you are both going?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I hope that you will enjoy Greece with Mr. Vyse."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Thank you."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "That's all right,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I counted on you two

keeping each other company. It's pouring again. The entire congregation,

which consists of your cousin, your mother, and my mother, stands

waiting in the church, till the carriage fetches it. Did Powell go

round?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I think so; I'll see."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No--of course, I'll see. How are the Miss Alans?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Very well, thank you."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Did you tell Mr. Emerson about Greece?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I--I did."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Don't you think it very plucky of her, Mr. Emerson, to undertake the

two Miss Alans? Now, Miss Honeychurch, go back--keep warm. I think three

is such a courageous number to go travelling."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "He is not going,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I made a slip. Mr. Vyse does stop

behind in England."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"You are leaving

him? You are leaving the man you love?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I--I had to."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Why, Miss Honeychurch, why?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"My dear, I am worried about you. It seems to

me"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "that you are in a muddle."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Take an old man's word; there's nothing worse than a muddle in all the

world. It is easy to face Death and Fate, and the things that sound

so dreadful. It is on my muddles that I look back with horror--on the

things that I might have avoided. We can help one another but little. I

used to think I could teach young people the whole of life, but I know

better now, and all my teaching of George has come down to this: beware

of muddle. Do you remember in that church, when you pretended to be

annoyed with me and weren't? Do you remember before, when you refused

the room with the view? Those were muddles--little, but ominous--and I

am fearing that you are in one now."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Don't trust me,

Miss Honeychurch. Though life is very glorious, it is difficult."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"'Life' wrote a friend of mine, 'is a public

performance on the violin, in which you must learn the instrument as you

go along.' I think he puts it well. Man has to pick up the use of his

functions as he goes along--especially the function of Love."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "That's it; that's what I mean. You love George!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "But you do,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"You love the

boy body and soul, plainly, directly, as he loves you, and no other word

expresses it. You won't marry the other man for his sake."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "How dare you!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Oh, how like a man!--I mean, to suppose that a woman is always thinking

about a man."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "But you are."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"You're shocked, but I mean to shock you. It's the only hope at times. I

can reach you no other way. You must marry, or your life will be wasted.

You have gone too far to retreat. I have no time for the tenderness, and

the comradeship, and the poetry, and the things that really matter, and

for which you marry. I know that, with George, you will find them, and

that you love him. Then be his wife. He is already part of you. Though

you fly to Greece, and never see him again, or forget his very name,

George will work in your thoughts till you die. It isn't possible to

love and to part. You will wish that it was. You can transmute love,

ignore it, muddle it, but you can never pull it out of you. I know by

experience that the poets are right: love is eternal."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I only wish poets would say this, too: love is of the body; not

the body, but of the body. Ah! the misery that would be saved if we

confessed that! Ah! for a little directness to liberate the soul! Your

soul, dear Lucy! I hate the word now, because of all the cant with which

superstition has wrapped it round. But we have souls. I cannot say how

they came nor whither they go, but we have them, and I see you ruining

yours. I cannot bear it. It is again the darkness creeping in; it

is hell."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"What nonsense I have talked--how

abstract and remote! And I have made you cry! Dear girl, forgive my

prosiness; marry my boy. When I think what life is, and how seldom love

is answered by love--Marry him; it is one of the moments for which the

world was made."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Then, Lucy--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You've frightened me,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Cecil--Mr. Beebe--the ticket's

bought--everything."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I'm caught in

the tangle. I must suffer and grow old away from him. I cannot break the

whole of life for his sake. They trusted me."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Give George my love--once only. Tell him 'muddle.'"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Lucy--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No--they are in the hall--oh, please not, Mr. Emerson--they trust me--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "But why should they, when you have deceived them?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Here's my mother."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You're not worthy of their trust."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What's that?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I was saying, why should you trust her when she deceived you?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "One minute, mother."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I don't follow you, Mr. Emerson. To whom do you refer? Trust whom?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I mean she has pretended to you that she did not love George. They have

loved one another all along."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I shall never marry him,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Why not?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Mr. Beebe--I have misled you--I have misled myself--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, rubbish, Miss Honeychurch!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It is not rubbish!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"It's the part of people

that you don't understand."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Lucy! Lucy!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Mr. Beebe, could you help me?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I

am more grieved than I can possibly express. It is lamentable,

lamentable--incredible."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What's wrong with the boy?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Nothing, Mr. Emerson, except that he no longer interests me. Marry

George, Miss Honeychurch. He will do admirably."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Lucy!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Now it is all dark. Now Beauty and Passion seem never to have existed.

I know. But remember the mountains over Florence and the view. Ah, dear,

if I were George, and gave you one kiss, it would make you brave. You

have to go cold into a battle that needs warmth, out into the muddle

that you have made yourself; and your mother and all your friends

will despise you, oh, my darling, and rightly, if it is ever right to

despise. George still dark, all the tussle and the misery without a word

from him. Am I justified?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Yes, for we

fight for more than Love or Pleasure; there is Truth. Truth counts,

Truth does count."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You kiss me,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You kiss me. I will try."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "never exactly understood,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"how he

managed to strengthen her. It was as if he had made her see the whole of

everything at once."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No, it isn't,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"because it is the room I had, and I had your

father's room. I forget why; Charlotte made me, for some reason."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "George, you baby, get up."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Why shouldn't I be a baby?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, bother Charlotte,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"What can such people be

made of?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Same stuff as parsons are made of."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Nonsense!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Quite right. It is nonsense."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Now you get up off the cold floor, or you'll be starting rheumatism

next, and you stop laughing and being so silly."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Why shouldn't I laugh?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What's there to cry at? Kiss me here."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Any letters?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Just a line from Freddy."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Now kiss me here; then here."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Lucy, you come and look at the cypresses; and the church, whatever its

name is, still shows."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "San Miniato. I'll just finish your sock."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Signorino, domani faremo uno giro,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Anything good in Freddy's letter?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Not yet."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What does he say?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Silly boy! He thinks he's being dignified. He knew we should go off in

the spring--he has known it for six months--that if mother wouldn't give

her consent we should take the thing into our own hands. They had fair

warning, and now he calls it an elopement. Ridiculous boy--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Signorino, domani faremo uno giro--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"But it will all come right in the end. He has to build us both up

from the beginning again. I wish, though, that Cecil had not turned so

cynical about women. He has, for the second time, quite altered. Why

will men have theories about women? I haven't any about men. I wish,

too, that Mr. Beebe--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You may well wish that."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"He will never forgive us--I mean, he will never be interested in us

again. I wish that he did not influence them so much at Windy Corner. I

wish he hadn't--But if we act the truth, the people who really love us

are sure to come back to us in the long run."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Perhaps."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Well, I acted the truth--the

only thing I did do--and you came back to me. So possibly you know."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Nonsense with that sock."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Signorino, domani faremo--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, bother that man!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"No, don't be

rude to him."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Mr.

Eager and Charlotte, dreadful frozen Charlotte. How cruel she would be

to a man like that!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Look at the lights going over the bridge."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"But this room reminds me of Charlotte. How horrible to grow old in

Charlotte's way! To think that evening at the rectory that she shouldn't

have heard your father was in the house. For she would have stopped me

going in, and he was the only person alive who could have made me see

sense. You couldn't have made me. When I am very happy"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"I remember on how little it all hangs. If Charlotte had only

known, she would have stopped me going in, and I should have gone to

silly Greece, and become different for ever."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "But she did know,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"she did see my father, surely. He said

so."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Oh, no, she didn't see him. She was upstairs with old Mrs. Beebe, don't

you remember, and then went straight to the church. She said so."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "My father,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"saw her, and I prefer

his word. He was dozing by the study fire, and he opened his eyes,

and there was Miss Bartlett. A few minutes before you came in. She was

turning to go as he woke up. He didn't speak to her."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"It's clear that she knew. Then, why

did she risk the meeting? She knew he was there, and yet she went to

church."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"How like Charlotte to undo her work by a feeble

muddle at the last moment."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Or did she mean it?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Mean what?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Signorino, domani faremo uno giro--"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Lascia, prego, lascia.

Siamo sposati."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Scusi tanto, signora,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Buona sera--e grazie."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Niente."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Mean what, George?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text:
"Is it this? Is this possible? I'll put a marvel to you.

That your cousin has always hoped. That from the very first moment we

met, she hoped, far down in her mind, that we should be like this--of

course, very far down. That she fought us on the surface, and yet she

hoped. I can't explain her any other way. Can you? Look how she kept me

alive in you all the summer; how she gave you no peace; how month after

month she became more eccentric and unreliable. The sight of us haunted

her--or she couldn't have described us as she did to her friend. There

are details--it burnt. I read the book afterwards. She is not frozen,

Lucy, she is not withered up all through. She tore us apart twice, but

in the rectory that evening she was given one more chance to make us

happy. We can never make friends with her or thank her. But I do believe

that, far down in her heart, far below all speech and behaviour, she is

glad."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It is impossible,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No--it is just possible."
quotes.speaker: Unknown
